name: gizza-ai/ecies-encrypt
summary: Encrypt or decrypt ECIES messages with secp256k1, P-256, or P-384

tool.description: Encrypt or decrypt ECIES hybrid payloads. Encryption accepts a recipient elliptic-curve public key, derives an ephemeral ECDH shared secret, expands it with HKDF-SHA256, and seals data with AES-256-GCM or XChaCha20-Poly1305. Decryption accepts the matching private key and verifies the AEAD tag before returning plaintext. Supports secp256k1, p256 and p384; SEC1 hex/base64 and PEM keys; ecies.py/ecies.js-compatible payload layout; and deterministic nonce/ephemeral-key fields for test vectors.

cipher.description: Symmetric AEAD used after ECDH+HKDF: AES-256-GCM (default) or XChaCha20-Poly1305.

compressed_ephemeral.description: When encrypting, store the ephemeral public key compressed (33/49 bytes) instead of uncompressed SEC1. Decryption auto-detects either shape.

curve.description: Elliptic curve for the recipient key: secp256k1 (default), p256/prime256v1, or p384.

data.description: For encrypt: plaintext (auto/text default) or bytes encoded as hex/base64. For decrypt: the ECIES payload, usually base64 or hex.

data_encoding.description: How to decode data. Auto means text while encrypting and base64 while decrypting.

ephemeral_key.description: Optional deterministic ephemeral private key for reproducible tests. Leave blank in normal use so a fresh key is generated.

kdf_input.description: HKDF input convention: ephemeral-and-point matches ecies.py/ecies.js; shared-x uses only the ECDH shared X coordinate.

key.description: For encrypt: recipient public key. For decrypt: recipient private key. Accepts SEC1 hex/base64 or PEM when key_encoding=auto/pem.

key_encoding.description: How to decode key and ephemeral_key: auto (detect PEM/hex/base64), hex, base64, or pem.

nonce.description: Optional nonce as hex or base64. Leave blank for a fresh random nonce during encryption. Ignored during decryption because the payload carries its nonce.

nonce_length.description: Nonce length in bytes. AES-256-GCM accepts 16 (ecies.py/ecies.js default) or 12 (NIST standard); XChaCha20-Poly1305 uses 24.

operation.description: Operation to perform: encrypt plaintext to a recipient public key, or decrypt an ECIES payload with the matching private key.

output_encoding.description: How to encode binary encryption payloads and non-UTF-8 plaintext on decrypt: base64 (default) or hex.
